texts.full_text: primitive neuroectodermal tumour. A case report and review of the literature. A 19-year-old woman presented with left-sided sensorineural hearing loss. She was found to have an enhancing mass in her right cerebellopontine angle on MRI, which is consistent with a vestibular schwannoma (VS). The VS resection via middle cranial fossa approach and tumor decompression of the internal auditory canal were performed. Postoperative histopathological examination revealed adult primitive neuroectodermal tumour (PNET) instead of typical VS. Case Report A 19-year-old woman presented with sudden onset left-sided sensorineural hearing loss, which progressed over a week to complete deafness in the affected ear and severe vertigo. She also reported episodes of nausea without vomiting but no headache or visual disturbances at presentation. The patient had an unremarkable medical history. On examination, she was alert with normal cranial nerve function except for absent hearing on her left side (left-sided sensorineural deafness) confirmed by audiometry and speech discrimination tests. No cerebellar signs were observed during the neurological assessment. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), including contrast enhancement revealed a 1 cm enhancing mass at right cerebellopontine angle with internal auditory canal involvement. The patient underwent resection of vestibular schwannoma via middle cranial fossa approach and tumor decompression of the internal acoustic meatus. The operative report confirmed complete removal, but postoperative histopathological examination revealed a primitive neuroectodermal tumour (PNET) instead of typical VS. Discussion Vestibulocochlear nerve tumors are mostly benign lesions that arise from Schwann cells or endoneural microvascular pericytes. They represent 5-10% of all intracranial neoplasms and account for approximately 80–90 % of cerebellopontine angle (CPA) masses. Vestibular schwannoma is the most common tumor in this location, accounting for about 75 percent to 85 percent. The diagnosis usually made by MRI with contrast enhancement showing a well-defined mass that enhances uniformly and has hypointense signal on T2-weighted images relative to brain parenchyma. Let go, and that current you worship will throw you tumbled and smashed against the rocks, and you will die quicker than boredom!" But the one heeded them not, and taking a breath did let go, and at once was tumbled and smashed by the current across the rocks. Yet in time, as the creature refused to cling again, the current lifted him free from the bottom, and he was bruised and hurt no more.
